### Problem Statement
MCP just released a new specification with the ability to have long running tasks, and to poll for results with a taskId. Without this feature, it is quite complex to handle long running tasks.
See https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/issues/1686 and https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/1732
### Proposed Solution
Implement Task handling in the `MCPClient`.
At the moment the MCP python SDK is not fully ready, see https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/1645
### Use Case
When agent needs MCP tools that take too long to answer synchronously (long data processing for example), the agent would trigger the task and then poll the server to know when a task is finished.
### Alternatives Solutions
Manually handle a set of tools (start / poll / get_result)

169     def start(self) -> "MCPClient":
170         """Starts the background thread and waits for initialization.
171 
172         This method starts the background thread that manages the MCP connection
173         and blocks until the connection is ready or times out.
174 
175         Returns:
176             self: The MCPClient instance
177 
178         Raises:
179             Exception: If the MCP connection fails to initialize within the timeout period
180         """
181         if self._is_session_active():
182             raise MCPClientInitializationError("the client session is currently running")
183 
184         self._log_debug_with_thread("entering MCPClient context")
185         # Copy context vars to propagate to the background thread
186         # This ensures that context set in the main thread is accessible in the background thread
187         # See: https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python/issues/1440
188         ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
189         self._background_thread = threading.Thread(target=ctx.run, args=(self._background_task,), daemon=True)
190         self._background_thread.start()
191         self._log_debug_with_thread("background thread started, waiting for ready event")
192         try:
193             # Blocking main thread until session is initialized in other thread or if the thread stops
194             self._init_future.result(timeout=self._startup_timeout)
195             self._log_debug_with_thread("the client initialization was successful")
196         except futures.TimeoutError as e:
197             logger.exception("client initialization timed out")
198             # Pass None for exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb since this isn't a context manager exit
199             self.stop(None, None, None)
200             raise MCPClientInitializationError(
201                 f"background thread did not start in {self._startup_timeout} seconds"
202             ) from e
203         except Exception as e:
204             logger.exception("client failed to initialize")
205             # Pass None for exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb since this isn't a context manager exit
206             self.stop(None, None, None)
207             raise MCPClientInitializationError("the client initialization failed") from e
208         return self

305     def stop(self, exc_type: BaseException | None, exc_val: BaseException | None, exc_tb: TracebackType | None) -> None:
306         """Signals the background thread to stop and waits for it to complete, ensuring proper cleanup of all resources.
307 
308         This method is defensive and can handle partial initialization states that may occur
309         if start() fails partway through initialization.
310 
311         Resources to cleanup:
312         - _background_thread: Thread running the async event loop
313         - _background_thread_session: MCP ClientSession (auto-closed by context manager)
314         - _background_thread_event_loop: AsyncIO event loop in background thread
315         - _close_future: AsyncIO future to signal thread shutdown
316         - _close_exception: Exception that caused the background thread shutdown; None if a normal shutdown occurred.
317         - _init_future: Future for initialization synchronization
318 
319         Cleanup order:
320         1. Signal close future to background thread (if session initialized)
321         2. Wait for background thread to complete
322         3. Reset all state for reuse
323 
324         Args:
325             exc_type: Exception type if an exception was raised in the context
326             exc_val: Exception value if an exception was raised in the context
327             exc_tb: Exception traceback if an exception was raised in the context
328         """
329         self._log_debug_with_thread("exiting MCPClient context")
330 
331         # Only try to signal close future if we have a background thread
332         if self._background_thread is not None:
333             # Signal close future if event loop exists
334             if self._background_thread_event_loop is not None:
335 
336                 async def _set_close_event() -> None:
337                     if self._close_future and not self._close_future.done():
338                         self._close_future.set_result(None)
339 
340                 # Not calling _invoke_on_background_thread since the session does not need to exist
341                 # we only need the thread and event loop to exist.
342                 asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro=_set_close_event(), loop=self._background_thread_event_loop)
343 
344             self._log_debug_with_thread("waiting for background thread to join")
345             self._background_thread.join()
346 
347         if self._background_thread_event_loop is not None:
348             self._background_thread_event_loop.close()
349 
350         self._log_debug_with_thread("background thread is closed, MCPClient context exited")
351 
352         # Reset fields to allow instance reuse
353         self._init_future = futures.Future()
354         self._background_thread = None
355         self._background_thread_session = None
356         self._background_thread_event_loop = None
357         self._session_id = uuid.uuid4()
358         self._loaded_tools = None
359         self._tool_provider_started = False
360         self._consumers = set()
361 
362         if self._close_exception:
363             exception = self._close_exception
364             self._close_exception = None
365             raise RuntimeError("Connection to the MCP server was closed") from exception

664     async def _async_background_thread(self) -> None:
665         """Asynchronous method that runs in the background thread to manage the MCP connection.
666 
667         This method establishes the transport connection, creates and initializes the MCP session,
668         signals readiness to the main thread, and waits for a close signal.
669         """
670         self._log_debug_with_thread("starting async background thread for MCP connection")
671 
672         # Initialized here so that it has the asyncio loop
673         self._close_future = asyncio.Future()
674 
675         try:
676             async with self._transport_callable() as (read_stream, write_stream, *_):
677                 self._log_debug_with_thread("transport connection established")
678                 async with ClientSession(
679                     read_stream,
680                     write_stream,
681                     message_handler=self._handle_error_message,
682                     elicitation_callback=self._elicitation_callback,
683                 ) as session:
684                     self._log_debug_with_thread("initializing MCP session")
685                     await session.initialize()
686 
687                     self._log_debug_with_thread("session initialized successfully")
688                     # Store the session for use while we await the close event
689                     self._background_thread_session = session
690                     # Signal that the session has been created and is ready for use
691                     self._init_future.set_result(None)
692 
693                     self._log_debug_with_thread("waiting for close signal")
694                     # Keep background thread running until signaled to close.
695                     # Thread is not blocked as this a future
696                     await self._close_future
697 
698                     self._log_debug_with_thread("close signal received")
699         except Exception as e:
700             # If we encounter an exception and the future is still running,
701             # it means it was encountered during the initialization phase.
702             if not self._init_future.done():
703                 self._init_future.set_exception(e)
704             else:
705                 # _close_future is automatically cancelled by the framework which doesn't provide us with the useful
706                 # exception, so instead we store the exception in a different field where stop() can read it
707                 self._close_exception = e
708                 if self._close_future and not self._close_future.done():
709                     self._close_future.set_result(None)
710 
711                 self._log_debug_with_thread(
712                     "encountered exception on background thread after initialization %s", str(e)
713                 )
714

726     def _background_task(self) -> None:

729         This method creates a new event loop for the background thread,
730         sets it as the current event loop, and runs the async_background_thread
731         coroutine until completion. In this case "until completion" means until the _close_future is resolved.
